title: Normalized additive derived tensor constraints from resolving models
statement:
Let $(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$ be a ringed site small relative to the universe of its ordinary module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], with $\mathcal O$ commutative. Use integer-indexed cochain complexes, $E[a]^p=E^{p+a}$ and $d_{E[a]}=(-1)^a d_E$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and the direct-sum total tensor $T(E,F)$ with differential $d(x\otimes y)=dx\otimes y+(-1)^p x\otimes dy$ [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves].

Let $q:K(\mathcal O)\to D(\mathcal O)$ be homotopy-category localization, and let $\mathcal P$ be its full subcategory of K-flat complexes with flat terms [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. Fix the actual derived tensor and its natural representative comparison
$$r_{E,F}:qT(E,F)\xrightarrow{\sim}qE\otimes^LqF\qquad(E,F\in\mathcal P)$$
of [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent]. The class $\mathcal P$ is closed under total tensor [lem-pur-kflat-total-tensor-model], every integer shift [lem-weil-pbc-kflat-fixed-tensor-triangulated], and finite direct sums. A flat sheaf in degree zero belongs to $\mathcal P$ [lem-pc-kflat-closure]; for flat sheaves $P,Q$, the ordinary sheaf $P\otimes_{\mathcal O}Q$ is flat and $P[0]\otimes^LQ[0]\cong(P\otimes_{\mathcal O}Q)[0]$ by the representative comparison.

There exist unique derived natural isomorphisms $t_{a,b}$, $\alpha$, and $\sigma$ normalized by $r$ and the localization shift comparisons as follows: on resolving pairs, $t_{a,b}$ is the localization of the chain map multiplying $E[a]^p\otimes F[b]^q$ by $(-1)^{bp}$; on resolving triples $\alpha$ is the localization of unsigned reassociation; on resolving pairs $\sigma$ is the localization of $x\otimes y\mapsto(-1)^{pq}y\otimes x$. Uniqueness refers to natural isomorphisms having these representative squares, rather than to arbitrary isomorphisms of their object values.

For any finite number of variables, restriction along resolving representatives is fully faithful on the category of functors from the corresponding product of derived categories into any category. Consequently every equality of natural transformations built from these tensor and shift functors is equivalent to its equality on resolving tuples, with all representative comparisons inserted. This applies in particular to ternary associativity and binary signed symmetry diagrams.

The fixed derived tensor is additive separately in both variables on all derived morphisms. More precisely, tensoring sends each binary biproduct inclusion/projection diagram to a biproduct diagram; hence for parallel derived maps $v,w$ and a fixed derived object $H$ one has $(v+w)\otimes^L1_H=(v\otimes^L1_H)+(w\otimes^L1_H)$, and likewise in the second variable. These assertions impose no boundedness or flatness on the derived objects.

source.place: Tag 0FPT (lemma-symmetric-monoidal-derived), together with lemma-tensor-product-K-flat and definition-derived-tor. Agent-formulated normalized resolving-localization and additive-constraint refinement; includes the details omitted in the symmetric-monoidal proof.

proof.text: First check that all iterated models used below are resolving. By [lem-pur-kflat-total-tensor-model], $T(E,F)$ is K-flat with flat terms for $E,F\in\mathcal P$. By [lem-weil-pbc-kflat-fixed-tensor-triangulated], every $E[a]$ is in $\mathcal P$. By [lem-pc-kflat-closure], K-flat complexes and flat sheaves are closed under countable direct sums, hence finite sums (extend the finite family by zero objects). The same lemma puts every flat sheaf $P[0]$ in $\mathcal P$. Apply the total-tensor model theorem to $P[0],Q[0]$: its degree-zero term $P\otimes_{\mathcal O}Q$ is flat, and all other terms are zero. The specified representative comparison $r$ therefore gives $P[0]\otimes^LQ[0]\cong(P\otimes_{\mathcal O}Q)[0]$.

proof.text: Put $L=q|_{\mathcal P}$ and let $W$ be the quasi-isomorphisms in $\mathcal P$. The equivalence $W^{-1}\mathcal P\simeq D(\mathcal O)$ of [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] makes $L$ a localization in the universal-property sense of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property]: factor through $\mathcal P\to W^{-1}\mathcal P$ and compose with that equivalence; precomposition with an equivalence has a quasi-inverse given by precomposition with its inverse. For each finite set $J$, [lem-sfb-product-localization] now makes $L^J$ a localization, since $W$ contains identities. The natural-transformation clauses (2) and (3) of the universal-property node say exactly that precomposition with $L^J$ is full and faithful on functors $(D(\mathcal O))^J\to\mathcal E$. In particular every natural transformation on the restrictions extends uniquely, and inverses extend to inverses by compatibility with identities and composition. This includes $J=\varnothing$, when both products are terminal categories.

proof.text: Use the natural chain isomorphisms of [lem-pur-total-tensor-signed-coherence]: $t^{\rm Ch}_{a,b}$ multiplies the shifted bidegree $(p,q)$ by $(-1)^{bp}$, $\alpha^{\rm Ch}$ reassociates without a sign, and $\sigma^{\rm Ch}$ has sign $(-1)^{pq}$. Their inverses are given there as well. Localize these maps and insert $r$ and the localization shift comparisons of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Naturality on $\mathcal P$ follows from chain naturality: every homotopy-category morphism is a homotopy class of a chain map, and the given tensor and $r$ are natural on those homotopy classes by [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent]. Step 1 ensures that shifted and iterated arguments of $r$ are in its stated domain. The next two steps spell out the resulting representative transformations before extending them by Step 2.

proof.text:
For a resolving triple define comparisons, with composition read right to left,
$$A_L=(r_{E,F}\otimes^L1_{qG})\circ r_{T(E,F),G},\qquad A_R=(1_{qE}\otimes^Lr_{F,G})\circ r_{E,T(F,G)}.$$
Their targets are $(qE\otimes^LqF)\otimes^LqG$ and $qE\otimes^L(qF\otimes^LqG)$, respectively. Thus the representative associator is exactly
$$A_R\circ q(\alpha^{\rm Ch}_{E,F,G})\circ A_L^{-1}.$$
All factors are natural isomorphisms by [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] and [lem-pur-total-tensor-signed-coherence]. Apply Step 2 for three variables to this transformation and its inverse. This constructs a derived natural isomorphism $\alpha$ with precisely the required square; faithfulness makes it the unique such natural isomorphism.

proof.text:
Write $e_{E,a}:q(E[a])\xrightarrow{\sim}(qE)[a]$ for the fixed localization shift comparison of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. On resolving pairs form
$$t_{a,b}=r_{E,F}[a+b]\circ e_{T(E,F),a+b}\circ q(t^{\rm Ch}_{a,b})\circ r_{E[a],F[b]}^{-1}\circ(e_{E,a}^{-1}\otimes^Le_{F,b}^{-1}),$$
This is a map $(qE)[a]\otimes^L(qF)[b]\to(qE\otimes^LqF)[a+b]$. Similarly the representative symmetry is
$$r_{F,E}\circ q(\sigma^{\rm Ch}_{E,F})\circ r_{E,F}^{-1}.$$
The comparisons $r$ are those of [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent], and the chain maps and their inverses are those of [lem-pur-total-tensor-signed-coherence]. These formulas are natural isomorphisms between the restrictions of the desired derived functors. Step 2 for two variables extends each and its inverse uniquely. They give the asserted $t_{a,b}$ and $\sigma$ with their fixed signs; uniqueness is relative to the displayed comparisons, as required.

proof.text: For any two composites of the resulting natural transformations, restriction is compatible with composition and identities. By the faithfulness proved in Step 2, the composites agree if and only if their restrictions agree. Substituting the formulas in Steps 4 and 5 identifies those restrictions with the corresponding localized chain diagrams with all $r$ and shift comparisons inserted. This proves the asserted equality test, including ternary associativity and binary signed symmetry diagrams. It tests natural transformations, not unrelated isomorphisms between individual objects.

proof.text:
Fix any derived object $H$. The resolving localization equivalence of [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] provides $E\in\mathcal P$ and an isomorphism $u:qE\xrightarrow{\sim}H$. By [lem-weil-pbc-kflat-fixed-tensor-triangulated], the fixed tensor functors $-\otimes^LqE$ and $qE\otimes^L-$ are exact on the entire unbounded derived category. Exact functors are additive by [def-weil-triangulated-category]. Tensoring $u$ gives natural isomorphisms from these two functors to $-\otimes^LH$ and $H\otimes^L-$, respectively. Explicitly, for the first functor write $c_K=1_K\otimes^Lu$. Naturality gives
$$F_H(v)=c_L\circ F_{qE}(v)\circ c_K^{-1}\quad(v:K\to L).$$
Hence bilinearity of composition in the additive category $D(\mathcal O)$ gives
$$F_H(v+w)=c_L(F_{qE}(v)+F_{qE}(w))c_K^{-1}=F_H(v)+F_H(w).$$
The same calculation with $c_K=u\otimes^L1_K$ proves additivity in the other variable. All maps $v,w$ here are arbitrary derived morphisms; no assertion that they are represented by chain maps between the chosen models is used.

proof.text: To verify the stated biproduct diagrams explicitly, let $i_j:X_j\to B$, $p_j:B\to X_j$ be a binary biproduct in $D(\mathcal O)$. They satisfy $p_ji_k=\delta_{jk}$ and $i_1p_1+i_2p_2=1_B$. Each fixed tensor functor $F$ preserves compositions, identities and, by Step 7, sums and zero maps. The images therefore satisfy the same two identities. For maps $f_j:Y\to F(X_j)$ the unique map to $F(B)$ is $F(i_1)f_1+F(i_2)f_2$, as follows by composing with the $F(p_j)$; uniqueness follows by multiplying by $\sum_jF(i_j)F(p_j)=1$. Dually the unique map out of $F(B)$ with restrictions $g_j$ is $g_1F(p_1)+g_2F(p_2)$. Thus the actual images of the inclusions and projections are a biproduct diagram. Step 7 gives the displayed sum identities of the item. All resolving and exactness inputs used above allow complexes unbounded in both directions, so no extra boundedness or flatness hypothesis has entered.
